summary:
Map each guide value to its position. Sort the items by the key (guide position, or one past the end if the
value isn't in the guide; then the value itself). Guide values come out in guide order with repeats together,
and the rest come after in increasing order. O((n + g) log n).

question.md:
Order `items` so values that appear in `guide` come first, in guide order (copies together), and all other values
follow in increasing order.

- **Guide values are distinct**; items can repeat.
- **Up to 10⁵ items and guide entries**, values up to 10⁹.

think.md:
Items `[5, 9, 2, 7, 9, 4, 5, 1]`, guide `[9, 5, 3]`. First both 9s, then both 5s; the guide's 3 isn't among the items, so it
contributes nothing. Then 1, 2, 4, 7 in order. Answer: `[9, 9, 5, 5, 1, 2, 4, 7]`.

Any custom order is just a sort with the right **key**. Here the key is a pair: first the value's place in the
guide (values not in the guide all share the place "after the guide"), then the value itself to order those
leftovers.

approaches.title: Pull matches for each guide value

idea.md: For each guide value in order, scan the items and move every match to the output. Sort what's left and append it.

build: For each guide value, scan all items for matches.
Sort the unused items and append.

lines.text: The output, and which items have been placed.
Guide values in order: every matching item goes out, so copies stay together.
Items not in the guide, sorted, go last.

complexity.md: **Time O(n·g + n log n):** a full scan of the items for every guide value, up to 10¹⁰. **Space O(n).**

steps.text: Guide value 9: scan all items, take 2 match(es).
Guide value 5: scan all items, take 2 match(es).
Guide value 3: scan all items, take 0 match(es).

walk.title: Walk the guide; for each guide value, pull every matching item. Then sort whatever is left.

limits.md: Each guide value rescans every item. Instead, look up each item's guide position once (a hash map) and let a single sort place everything.

idea.md: Build `rank[value] = position in guide`. Sort items by `(rank.get(x, g), x)`: values not in the guide all get rank `g`, after every guide value, and are then ordered by value.

lines.text: Each guide value's position. Values not in the guide get `g`, which sorts after all of them.

notes.c: No hash map in C: sort the guide's (value, position) pairs by value and look values up with `bsearch`.

lines.text: One sort by the pair (rank, value) puts guide values in guide order and the rest in increasing order after them.

notes.java: Sorting with a comparator needs boxed `Integer`s.
notes.c: Attach each item's rank, then sort by (rank, value).

complexity.md: **Time O(n log n + g).** **Space O(n + g).**

steps.text: Guide positions: {9: 0, 5: 1, 3: 2}. Values not in the guide get position 3 (after all of them).

walk.title: Give every value a sort key: (its position in the guide, or 'after the guide'; then the value itself). One sort does the rest.

takeaways.md:
- **Custom orders are sorts with a composite key.** Put the most important rule first in the tuple.
- Give "not in the list" a single rank larger than every listed one.
- In C, a sorted array plus `bsearch` stands in for a hash map lookup.
